topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself, sets the context within the cancer lecture series, and outlines the primary learning objectives.

topics.label: Conceptual frameworks and epidemiology of cancer causation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the interplay between intrinsic stochastic mutations, inherited predisposition, and environmental exposures in driving cancer development across populations.

topics.label: Infectious agents in carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how biological pathogens induce malignancy, featuring a detailed analysis of Epstein-Barr virus and Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and metabolic activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the biochemical pathways through which exogenous agents undergo metabolic conversion to induce direct and indirect DNA damage.

topics.label: Tumour promotion and host susceptibility factors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine non-mutagenic mechanisms that facilitate cancer outgrowth, focusing on tumor promotion, inflammatory microenvironments, and tissue developmental windows.

topics.label: Methods for identifying carcinogens and assessing risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine experimental, genomic, and epidemiological methodologies used to establish carcinogenicity and weigh exposure risks.

topics.label: Lecture summary and conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This section provides the lecturer's concluding remarks and final summary of the core principles covered in the lecture.
